description.value: The study examined whether motivation dispositions measured by BIS/BAS subscales modulate cognitive reappraisal-related emotional and neural responses differently in currently drug-free patients with major depressive disorder and healthy controls.

design.value: A block-designed fMRI study compared depressed patients and healthy controls during three consecutive emotion-regulation blocks: ATTEND as a baseline condition, DETACH as avoidance-oriented reappraisal, and IMMERSE as approach-oriented reappraisal. The order of DETACH and IMMERSE was counterbalanced across participants, and trials were randomized within blocks.

name.value: structured clinical interview for DSM-IV-TR Axis I (SCID I)

description.value: Participants were recruited and evaluated by structured clinical interview for DSM-IV-TR Axis I; patients were screened via diagnoses from an experienced psychiatric clinician according to DSM-IV-TR.

name.value: Behavioral Inhibition System and Behavioral Activation System Scale (BBS)

description.value: A revised Chinese version of the Behavioral Inhibition System and Behavioral Activation System Scale was administered immediately after the scan. The four-factor model included BIS, BASR, BASD, and BASF subscales.
BDI is a self-rating scale consisting of 21 items assessing emotional, cognitive, motivational and somatic symptoms, scored from 0 to 3.
SDS consists of 20 items assessing psychological and somatic symptoms, scored from 1 to 4.
HAMD-24 is an interview scale used to measure severity of depression.
Participants rated their emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale, from 1 = barely not to 4 = very strong, using four buttons on two fMRI-compatible joysticks.

task_description.value: The task was performed in three consecutive blocks: ATTEND, DETACH, and IMMERSE. During ATTEND, subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state elicited by the stimuli. During DETACH, participants interpreted the situation as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events. During IMMERSE, subjects perceived each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.

instructions.value: ATTEND: respond naturally without trying to change the emotional state. DETACH: interpret the situation depicted as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events. IMMERSE: perceive each picture as real by imagining yourself or a loved one in the scene.

stimuli.value: Pictures selected from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS), including positive, negative, and neutral affective images. Twenty-four trials were included in the detach/immerse condition and 36 trials in the attend condition; neutral pictures were only presented under attend.

task_performance_measures.value: self-reported ratings of emotional intensity on a 4-point Likert scale
elaboration on the strategies used after scanning to confirm the effectiveness of emotion regulation

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: A T1-weighted MPRAGE structural image was acquired with slice thickness = 4 mm, field of view = 240 × 240 × 240 mm3, and matrix = 256 × 256 × 256.

instrument.value: Siemens 3T Tim Trio MRI system (Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: Three functional sessions were acquired with a functional sequence using TR of 2,000 ms, flip angle of 90°, TE of 30 ms, FOV of 240 × 240 mm2, matrix of 64 × 64, slice thickness of 4 mm, and slice interval of 0.8 mm. Visual stimuli were presented through goggles mounted on the head coil.

The first trial of each block was discarded to reach magnetization equilibrium. Remaining volumes were corrected for slice timing, realigned to the mean volume to correct for head motion, spatially normalized to standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation, and smoothed with an 8-mm full-width at half-maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel.

steps.value: Discarded the first trial of each block to reach magnetization equilibrium.
Realignment to the mean volume to correct for head motion.

Smoothing by convolution with an 8-mm full-width at half-maximum isotropic Gaussian kernel.

description.value: Anatomically predefined ROI time courses were extracted by generating the first eigenvariate of 8 mm around peak voxels using REX.

steps.value: Defined bilateral dlPFC and vmPFC masks using WFU PickAtlas with a threshold of p < 0.05 and an extent threshold of 5 voxels.
Extracted the first eigenvariate of 8 mm around peak voxels from anatomically pre-defined ROIs.

model_type.value: whole-brain voxel-wise multiple linear regression model

model_settings.value: Each condition was modeled using a box-car function convolved with a canonical HRF. Realignment parameters were included as covariates of no interest.

Group, emotion and ER were entered as between-subject factors and BIS/BAS subscale scores as covariates. Interactive effects between group and motivation and the main effect of group on emotion regulation were examined.
A two-sample t-test was conducted with BIS/BAS scores as covariates to examine group-related differences in motivation.
For each group and each contrast (reappraisal vs. attend), BIS/BAS scores were entered as covariates of interest to identify clusters showing a linear relationship with BIS/BAS scores.
BBS subscale scores were compared between groups.

software.value: SPSS Version 19, SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA

model_settings.value: MANOVA tested whether motivational scores differed across groups and/or genders, including the gender-by-group interaction.

BIS/BAS scores were entered into a generalized linear regression model to predict reappraisal-related brain activation; BDI scores were additionally entered as a predictor in one depressed-patient model.
